mainTopic: The order of ברכות at קידוש and הבדלה, the order of spices and light, and a second ברכה on the כוס של ברכה
overview: The גמרא finishes listing opinions on the order of the ברכות when יום טוב starts on מוצאי שבת. The ברכות involved are יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, and later זמן. שמואל's father asks רבי, who answers with רבי יהושע בן חנניה's order נהי"ק. רבי חנינא explains that order with a parable: first escort out the departing king, then greet the arriving governor. The גמרא then asks for the practical ruling. אביי and רבא both follow רב's order and argue only about where זמן goes, and the הלכה follows רבא: יקנה"ז. Next comes a story: רבא blesses spices before light at הבדלה and is challenged from a משנה. He answers that רבי יהודה's version of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל supports him, and that רבי יוחנן reports the people's custom follows it. Finally, רב יעקב בר אבא asks why רבא says בורא פרי הגפן again on the כוס של ברכה. רבא's answer, a story about רב's students, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's order: wine, הבדלה, candle, קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the order is יהנ"ק: יין, הבדלה, נר, קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: י-ה-נ-ק (wine, הבדלה, candle, קידוש).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing a list of opinions, already begun on the previous amud, about the order of ברכות when יום טוב comes right after שבת. רבה gives his order as a memory code.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for one ברכה: י = יין, ה = הבדלה, נ = נר, ק = קידוש. רבה puts הבדלה before קידוש, so first we say goodbye to שבת and only then welcome יום טוב. He also says הבדלה before the candle, which is unusual.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory code made of initial letters
The blessing that separates holy time from the time that follows
The blessing that declares the holiness of the day, here יום טוב
The blessing over the flame (בורא מאורי האש)

steps.confusionAlert: The case is יום טוב falling on מוצאי שבת, so we need both קידוש for יום טוב and הבדלה for שבת on one cup. That is why the order matters at all.

phrases.english: And Rabba said: wine, havdala, candle, kiddush.
phrases.notes: יהנ״ק is a memory trick: each letter starts one step, in order: יין, הבדלה, נר, קידוש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of opinions (רב and שמואל) from the previous page.

steps.title: לוי's order and the רבנן's order
steps.stepSummary: לוי says קני"ה. The רבנן say קינ"ה. Both put קידוש first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: קידוש, candle, wine, הבדלה. And the רבנן say: קידוש, wine, candle, הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more opinions are added to the list. Both of them start with קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי and the רבנן agree that קידוש comes first and הבדלה comes last. They disagree only about the middle: לוי puts נר before יין, while the רבנן put יין before נר. Putting יין after קידוש is unusual, because normally the wine blessing comes first.

phrases.english: And Levi said: kiddush, candle, wine, havdala.
phrases.notes: Same kind of memory trick: ק-נ-י-ה, for קידוש, נר, יין, הבדלה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: kiddush, wine, candle, havdala.
phrases.notes: Another memory trick: ק-י-נ-ה, for קידוש, יין, נר, הבדלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further opinions to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי: קידוש, נר, יין, הבדלה. רבנן: קידוש, יין, נר, הבדלה.

steps.title: Two orders that start with the candle
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא says נקי"ה. מרתא, in the name of רבי יהושע, says ניה"ק.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבנא said: candle, קידוש, wine, הבדלה. מרתא said in the name of רבי יהושע: candle, wine, הבדלה, קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The last two opinions in the list are given. Both of them start with the candle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בריה דרבנא puts קידוש before הבדלה. מרתא's tradition from רבי יהושע puts הבדלה before קידוש, so שבת is ended before יום טוב begins. The next steps will bring a slightly different version of רבי יהושע's view.

phrases.english: Mar the son of Ravna said: candle, kiddush, wine, havdala.
phrases.notes: Another memory trick: נ-ק-י-ה, for נר, קידוש, יין, הבדלה.

phrases.english: Marta said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
Candle, wine, havdala, kiddush.
phrases.notes: Another memory trick: נ-י-ה-ק, for נר, יין, הבדלה, קידוש.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בריה דרבנא: נר, קידוש, יין, הבדלה. רבי יהושע (via מרתא): נר, יין, הבדלה, קידוש.

steps.title: שמואל's father asks רבי for the order
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל sends a letter to רבי asking how the ברכות should be ordered.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father sent to רבי: Let our teacher teach us, how is the order of the separations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. שמואל's father asks the leader of the generation, רבי יהודה הנשיא, for the correct order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With so many opinions in circulation, a direct question to רבי is natural. The phrase "order of הבדלות" means the order of the ברכות when יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Let our teacher teach us, a respectful way to ask a question

phrases.english: Shmuel's father sent to Rebbi:
Let our teacher teach us,
how is the order of the havdala blessings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a list of opinions to a direct inquiry to an authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct order of ברכות when יום טוב follows שבת.

steps.title: רבי answers with רבי יהושע בן חנניה's order
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers through a chain of tradition going back to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: נהי"ק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to him: So said רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, who said in the name of his father, who said in the name of רבי יהושע בן חנניה: candle, הבדלה, wine, קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question and supports it with a chain of teachers. The order is נר, הבדלה, יין, קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another version of רבי יהושע's view, slightly different from מרתא's ניה"ק. Both versions agree that הבדלה comes before קידוש, so שבת is ended first. The parable in the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father

phrases.english: He sent to him:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: So said Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
who said in the name of his father,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה:
phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
Candle, havdala, wine, kiddush.
phrases.notes: Another memory trick: נ-ה-י-ק, for נר, הבדלה, יין, קידוש.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: כָּךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of שמואל's father.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נר, הבדלה, יין, קידוש, according to רבי יהושע בן חנניה.

steps.title: The parable of the king leaving and the governor arriving
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains רבי יהושע בן חנניה's view with a parable: first escort out the king, then greet the governor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: The parable of רבי יהושע בן חנניה is like a king who is leaving and a governor who is entering. They escort the king, and afterward they go out to greet the governor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the reason behind putting הבדלה before קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is the king, with greater holiness, and יום טוב is the governor, with lesser holiness. Respect demands that we first escort the departing king (הבדלה for שבת) before welcoming the arriving governor (קידוש for יום טוב).

keyTerms.meaning: A governor, an official below the king

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reasoning of the opposing approach. The final הלכה (רב's order, as ruled by רבא) does not follow it and puts קידוש first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
The parable of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya
is like a king who is leaving and a governor who is entering,
they escort the king,
and afterward they go out to greet the governor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ending שבת (greater holiness) comes before welcoming יום טוב (lesser holiness).

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the practical conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: After all these opinions, the גמרא asks for the practical ruling. This line sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question turns the discussion from a list of views to practical הלכה. The answer will build on רב's order יקנ"ה and add the ברכה of זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of opinions to a request for the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical order of the ברכות.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about where to put the time blessing
steps.stepSummary: אביי says יקזנ"ה. רבא says יקנה"ז. Both follow רב's order and differ only on זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: wine, קידוש, זמן, candle, הבדלה. And רבא said: wine, קידוש, candle, הבדלה, זמן.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer. Both accept רב's order (יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה) and add the ברכה of זמן (שהחיינו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי puts זמן right after קידוש, because it belongs with welcoming the new יום טוב. רבא keeps רב's four ברכות together and puts זמן at the very end.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of שהחיינו, said for a new season or festival
אביי's code: יין, קידוש, זמן, נר, הבדלה
רבא's code: יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, זמן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי and רבא reopen the whole debate. They both accept that קידוש comes before הבדלה, as רב said, and argue only about זמן.

phrases.english: Abaye said: wine, kiddush, time, candle, havdala,
and Rava said: wine, kiddush, candle, havdala, time,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow רב's order. אביי adds זמן after קידוש; רבא adds it at the end.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבא
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like רבא: יקנה"ז.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is in accordance with רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical order is יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, זמן. This is the יקנה"ז printed in הגדות for a סדר that falls on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת, the order is יקנה"ז: יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, זמן.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Rava.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is יקנה"ז, following רבא.

steps.title: רבא blesses spices before light
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב הונא בר יהודה visits רבא, who makes the blessing on בשמים first and then on מאור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה came to רבא's house. After שבת they brought a light and spices. רבא blessed the spices first and then the light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבא's personal הבדלה practice. It is setting up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the order discussed was for יום טוב after שבת, where there are no בשמים. Now we are at a regular מוצאי שבת with both בשמים and a flame. רבא's order, spices first and then light, is what will be questioned.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda happened to come to Rava's house,
they brought before them a light and spices.
Rava blessed over the spices first
and then over the light.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יום טוב after שבת to the order of a regular מוצאי שבת הבדלה, using a story about רבא.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה: both schools put light first
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה objects that both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the light comes before the spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that light comes first and then spices!
steps.whatsHappening: The guest challenges רבא. He says that even though בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about other things, they agree that light comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both schools agree, there is no opinion that supports רבא's order. This makes רבא's practice look like it goes against everyone.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִילֵּל —
phrases.english: But both according to Beit Shammai and according to Beit Hillel —
light is first, and afterward the spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִילֵּל
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's order of בשמים before מאור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל put מאור first, so no opinion supports רבא's order.

steps.title: The משנה behind the challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: בית שמאי say נר, מזון, בשמים, הבדלה, and בית הלל say נר, בשמים, מזון, הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source? We learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say candle, meal-blessing, spices, הבדלה. בית הלל say candle, spices, meal-blessing, הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for רב הונא בר יהודה's claim. It quotes a משנה about someone who must say both ברכת המזון and הבדלה on one cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two schools argue about where ברכת המזון goes. In both lists, though, נר comes before בשמים. That shared detail is the proof against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is it? (asks for the source)
the blessing that separates holy from ordinary

steps.confusionAlert: Here מזון means ברכת המזון, not food. The case is someone finishing a meal as שבת ends, with only one cup of wine for both ברכת המזון and הבדלה.

phrases.english: And what is this? As we learned in a mishna:
Beit Shammai say:
Candle and Grace after Meals, spices and havdala.
And Beit Hillel say:
Candle and spices, and Grace after Meals and havdala.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual basis for the קשיא in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That both schools place נר before בשמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה (ברכות נא:): the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about one cup for מזון and הבדלה

steps.title: רבא: that is רבי מאיר's version; רבי יהודה reports otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. According to רבי יהודה, the two schools agree that מזון is first and הבדלה is last, and argue only about מאור and בשמים. בית הלל say בשמים first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא answered: This is רבי מאיר's version. But רבי יהודה says בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about ברכת המזון, which is first, or about הבדלה, which is last. What did they argue about? About light and spices. בית שמאי say light and then spices. בית הלל say spices and then light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. He says there is a second version of the dispute, from רבי יהודה, and in that version בית הלל put spices first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed there was only one version of the dispute. רבא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה report it differently. In רבי יהודה's version the whole argument is about מאור and בשמים, and בית הלל match רבא's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the statement of (only one opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are not giving their own rulings. Each one is reporting what בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about.

phrases.english: Rava answered after him and said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
but Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִילֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about Grace after Meals, that it is first,
or about havdala, that it is last.
About what did they disagree?
About the light and about the spices.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מָאוֹר וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּשָׂמִים,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: light and afterward spices,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִילֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּשָׂמִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָאוֹר.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: spices and afterward light.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָנֵי רָבָא בָּתְרֵיהּ וְאָמַר: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11 by limiting the משנה of Step 12 to רבי מאיר's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to one תנא and bringing a competing version (רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the only version of the dispute, so everyone puts מאור first.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבי יהודה's version, בית הלל say בשמים before מאור, which supports רבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the people follow בית הלל as רבי יהודה reports
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the accepted custom follows בית הלל according to רבי יהודה's version: בשמים before מאור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The people follow בית הלל, according to רבי יהודה's version.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by quoting רבי יוחנן's report of the accepted custom. This shows that רבא was simply following common practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that a version exists in which בית הלל put spices first is not enough by itself. רבי יוחנן adds that this version is the one people actually practice. That fully justifies רבא's order.

keyTerms.meaning: the people were accustomed / the custom is

steps.whatToRemember: On a regular מוצאי שבת, רבא blessed בשמים before מאור. This follows בית הלל as reported by רבי יהודה, and רבי יוחנן says that is the people's custom. In רבי מאיר's version of the משנה, both schools put the light first.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a practice that looks like it goes against a משנה can rest on another תנא's version of that same dispute, backed by accepted custom.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people were accustomed to follow Beit Hillel,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda's version.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נָהֲגוּ הָעָם כְּבֵית הִילֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יהודה's version from Step 13 is the accepted practice, closing the challenge to רבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The custom follows בית הלל per רבי יהודה: בשמים before מאור, as רבא did.

steps.title: רבא says the wine blessing twice
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא visits רבא and sees him say בורא פרי הגפן on the first cup and again on the כוס של ברכה after the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב בר אבא came to רבא's house. He saw רבא say 'Who creates the fruit of the vine' on the first cup. Then רבא said the same blessing again on the cup used for ברכת המזון, and drank it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. It is setting up a question about why רבא made the same ברכה twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בורא פרי הגפן at the start of a meal covers all the wine drunk during that meal. Here רבא makes a second בורא פרי הגפן on the כוס של ברכה after ברכת המזון. That second ברכה is what the next steps will question.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing over wine: 'Who creates the fruit of the vine'
The cup of blessing, the cup held during ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cups. The first is a regular cup drunk at the start of the meal. The second is the כוס של ברכה drunk after ברכת המזון. The whole question is about the blessing on the second cup.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov bar Abba happened to come to Rava's house,
he saw that he recited 'Who creates the fruit of the vine'
over the first cup,
and then he recited it again over the cup of blessing (after the meal),
phrases.notes: The cup used for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: and drank.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, like the story in Step 10 about a visit to רבא. This one is about ברכות on wine during a meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא recited בורא פרי הגפן both on the first cup and again on the כוס של ברכה.

steps.title: Why bless the wine a second time?
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא asks why רבא needed a second ברכה, since he already blessed on wine once.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why do you need all this? The Master already made the blessing for us one time!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יעקב בר אבא challenges רבא's practice. He says the second blessing seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that the first בורא פרי הגפן should cover all wine at the meal, including the כוס של ברכה. If so, a second ברכה would be a ברכה שאינה צריכה, an unnecessary blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do you need all this?
Master, a respectful way to address a rabbi

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לָךְ כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why do you need all this?

phrases.aramaic: הָא בָּרֵיךְ לַן מָר חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: The Master already blessed for us one time!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לָךְ כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's second בורא פרי הגפן on the כוס של ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברכה at the start of the meal covers all the wine, so the second ברכה looks unnecessary.

steps.title: That was the practice at the ריש גלותא's house
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this is what they used to do at the house of the ריש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When we were at the house of the ריש גלותא, this is what we did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by pointing to an existing custom. He says the ריש גלותא's household always made two ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not give a reason here. He only says this is an established practice among the rabbis at the ריש גלותא's table. That leaves room for the follow-up question about whether the custom fits his own home.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the leader of the Jews in Babylonia
This is what we used to do

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
phrases.english: He said to him: When we were at the house of the Exilarch,
this is what we did.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא הָכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows the practice at the ריש גלותא's house.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא's house is a different case
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא says the custom makes sense at the ריש גלותא's house, where guests never knew if more wine would come, but not here, where the cup is already in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It makes sense that at the ריש גלותא's house they act this way, because it is uncertain whether they will bring us more wine or not. But here, the cup is sitting in front of us and our mind is on it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יעקב בר אבא rejects the comparison. He argues that the ריש גלותא's custom has a special reason that does not apply at רבא's table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the ריש גלותא's house the guests depended on the host, so they never planned on more wine. Each new cup was a new decision and needed a new ברכה. At רבא's table the cup is right there and everyone intends to drink it, so the first ברכה should already cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well / that is understandable (for that case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether a ברכה covers later food or drink depends on דעת, what the person had in mind. If you planned on it, the first ברכה covers it. If you did not expect it, it may need a new ברכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תִּינַח בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
phrases.english: He said to him: It is understandable at the house of the Exilarch
that one acts this way,
since it is uncertain whether he will bring us (more wine)
or whether he will not bring us.
Here, the cup is resting in front of us
and our mind is on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תִּינַח בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא דְּהָכִי עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from the ריש גלותא's custom in Step 17 by showing that case is different.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the ריש גלותא's custom as a model for רבא's own table.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There, the guests were unsure more wine would come, so each cup needed a ברכה. Here, they were clearly planning to drink the cup, so the first ברכה covers it.

steps.title: רבא follows the students of רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he follows the practice of רב's students, and begins a story about רב ברונא and רב חננאל sitting at a meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I acted like the students of רב. For רב ברונא and רב חננאל, the students of רב, were sitting at a meal...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new source for his practice: the students of רב. He begins a story that will explain the reason, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending the ריש גלותא comparison, רבא switches to a different authority. The story about רב ברונא and רב חננאל is the setup. It will show why the second ברכה is needed even when the cup is in front of you.
steps.confusionAlert: The amud ends in the middle of a story. Do not look for the full answer yet. The reason for the second ברכה comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא עֲבַדִי כְּתַלְמִידֵי דְרַב,
phrases.english: He said to him: I acted in accordance with the students of Rav,
as Rav Beruna and Rav Chananel,
the students of Rav,
were sitting at a meal,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא עֲבַדִי כְּתַלְמִידֵי דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18's challenge with a new source after the ריש גלותא comparison was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New supporting authority (precedent from רב's students)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With the cup in front of us, the first ברכה should cover it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא relies on a precedent from רב's students. The details follow in the continuing story.
